rubric_items.reason: All 15 known REQs are traced. S-1 covers REQ-1 to 6 and 14, S-2 covers 7 and 8, S-3 covers 9 to 11 and 15, S-4 covers 12 and S-5 covers 13. The intent has no assumed REQs.
Most stories have one outcome. S-3 bundles three regression checks (paging, search and sort), and S-1 also carries REQ-14 (no highlight or filter).

The ACs are Given/When/Then and discriminating. They cover a time zone whose local and UTC dates differ, latest start vs latest closed, each excluded status, and duplicate rows in paging and search. S-5 AC1 only checks what is shown; S-3 AC3 does not say which sort order.
Asia/Kolkata and 20 per page come from the intent. UTC+05:30 and the UTC instants are derived inline. 21 patients follows from 20 per page. The dates and times are test data, not limits.
The terms are clear and match the glossary. The body summaries now match the front-matter criteria, including S-3 AC1.

findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (was F-3). S-5 AC1 only checks what is visible in the list. It would not catch medical history that is sent in the list's data but not displayed.

cites.quote: then none of the medical history values appear in the list, including in the Last visit column
No medical history appears in the patient list.

findings.suggested_fix: If REQ-13 covers list responses, add that the data behind the list also contains no medical history fields.

findings.text: S-3 AC3 does not name the current sort order or give concrete patients. A tester has to work out which order to expect, which makes the AC weaker as a check.

cites.quote: Given patients whose last visits are in a different order from the list's current sort order

findings.suggested_fix: Give two or three patients whose current sort order is the reverse of their Last visit order, and state the expected row order.

cites.quote: closed by staff once its start time has passed
An appointment that is booked and still open.
Blood group, allergies, chronic conditions, current medications and notes of one patient.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason

questions.text: Does REQ-13 ('No medical history appears in the patient list') also cover the data the list receives from the server, or only what is shown on screen?
